translationRepairs: Shi Yanbang, who held the south city, begged for relief and warned that missiles were almost gone.
Shi Yanshang, who held the south city, begged for relief and warned that missiles were almost gone.
氏延賞 is Shi Yanshang; Yanbang does not match the character 賞.
South-city defender Shi Yanbang reported urgency and said arrows and stones were nearly spent.
South-city defender Shi Yanshang reported urgency and said arrows and stones were nearly spent.
The literal field contains the same incorrect reading of 氏延賞 and must use Shi Yanshang.
In the seventh month Liu Yan and Yin Hao of Liang struck Tong.
In the seventh month Liu Xun and Yin Hao of Liang struck Tong.
劉鄩 is Liu Xun. Reading 鄩 as Yan is incorrect.
Autumn, seventh month, Liang generals Liu Yan and Yin Hao raided Tong prefecture.
Autumn, seventh month, Liang generals Liu Xun and Yin Hao raided Tong prefecture.
The literal field must likewise identify 劉鄩 as Liu Xun.
Liang sent Liu Yan and Yin Hao of Huazhou to invest Tong; Youqian cried for help, and Cunxu sent Li Cunshen as overall commander, Li Sizhao of Zhaoyi, and Wang Jianji of Dai to relieve him.
Liang sent Liu Xun and Yin Hao of Huazhou to invest Tong; Youqian cried for help, and Cunxu sent Li Cunshen as overall commander, Li Sizhao of Zhaoyi, and Wang Jianji of Dai to relieve him.
This is another occurrence of the same general Liu Xun, 劉鄩.

The Liang ruler then sent Liu Yan and Huazhou military commissioner Yin Hao with troops to besiege Tong; Youqian reported the crisis, and the Emperor sent Chinese-and-tribal overall commander Li Cunshen, Zhaoyi commissioner Li Sizhao, and Dai prefecture commissioner Wang Jianji with armies to the relief.

The Liang ruler then sent Liu Xun and Huazhou military commissioner Yin Hao with troops to besiege Tong; Youqian reported the crisis, and the Emperor sent Chinese-and-tribal overall commander Li Cunshen, Zhaoyi commissioner Li Sizhao, and Dai prefecture commissioner Wang Jianji with armies to the relief.
The paired literal occurrence of 劉鄩 must also read Liu Xun.
That night Liu Yan pulled the survivors into camp and never came out again.
That night Liu Xun pulled the survivors into camp and never came out again.
劉鄩 remains Liu Xun in this account of his retreat to camp.
Within days Yan slipped away by night.
Within days Xun slipped away by night.
The shortened 鄩 refers to Liu Xun and should be rendered Xun, not Yan.
After several days Yan fled by night.
After several days Xun fled by night.
The literal short form must use Xun for 鄩.
Jin caught them at the Wei; abandoned weapons and wagons littered the bank, while Yan and Yin rode off alone.
Jin caught them at the Wei; abandoned weapons and wagons littered the bank, while Xun and Yin rode off alone.
The two riders are Liu Xun and Yin Hao; Yan is the earlier misreading of 鄩.
The royal army caught them at the Wei River; abandoned arms, gear, and baggage were beyond counting, and Liu Yan and Yin Hao alone on horseback escaped.
The royal army caught them at the Wei River; abandoned arms, gear, and baggage were beyond counting, and Liu Xun and Yin Hao alone on horseback escaped.
The literal field must identify 劉鄩 as Liu Xun.
Soon Yan died of shame and rage.
Soon Xun died of shame and rage.
The shortened 鄩 in the death notice refers to Liu Xun.
Before long Yan died of grief and vexation that brought on illness.
Before long Xun died of grief and vexation that brought on illness.
The literal field must use Xun for the same shortened 鄩.
Li Cunxu of Youzhou became acting grand preceptor and joint director of the Secretariat, still overall commander of Tangut and Han horse and foot;
Li Cunshen of Youzhou became acting grand preceptor and joint director of the Secretariat, still overall commander of Tangut and Han horse and foot;
The named commissioner is 李存審, Li Cunshen, not Li Cunxu.
Youzhou military commissioner Li Cunxu was made acting grand preceptor and joint director of the Secretariat, continuing as overall commander of Tangut and Han horse and foot;
Youzhou military commissioner Li Cunshen was made acting grand preceptor and joint director of the Secretariat, continuing as overall commander of Tangut and Han horse and foot;
The literal field contains the same Cunshen/Cunxu identity error and should follow 李存審.
